title: Critique my movie review of The Substance (2024)

commenti.body: The movie was a lot of fun, but I had some issues with it. A little restraint in the beginning would have gone a long way, wuch as removing the dumb neighbor and Dennis Quaid, both of which do little beyond telegraphing what we already know. Likewise, the voiceover/flashbacks were obnoxious and did nothing more than help out audiences that are either dullards or only halfway paying attention. Moore was fantastic though, and I love weird place the movie went—and how determined it was to **really be** there.

I would shorten the plot summary. There's nothing wrong with summarizing plot points for a review, but I would cut it down so you can spend more time on your critiques and opinions of the film.

You touched on many important aspects of the film like cinematography, sound design, acting, and pacing. But I feel you could have expanded more on some of those critiques. 

I agree with your sentiment about the runtime too.

Thanks for the reply, I do have a lot to say about it in its technical elements and the way the story is told. My main focus that went into the writing is simplifying my thoughts are so it wouldn't fill up countless pages, so the review was basically a trimmed down and easy to read version of my initial critique.

I do like Dennis Quaid's character and presence in the film, he represents the very toxic mentality of treating women in the industry as some kind of toy to be played with and thrown away when it starts to age and you can how much DQ is enjoying that role on screen. However, the film presented him in the most obnoxious way leaving the character becoming too one-sided. I agree with the neighbor though, that's the only part of the movie that doesn't feel necessary or needed more time in the oven.

This review was written by deathclaw28.  It was clear from the review that they had seen The Substance and had thoughts about it.  Overall, I liked this review and would read it again.  

If possible, could someone please review my review of the review and offer some pointers?

I think reading the film as a critique of cosmetics or even cosmetic surgery is I think a bit shallow. In particular, the make-up scene before the date is genuinely one of my favorite parts of the movie because it's so relatable. The issue isn't the make-up of course because she actually looks great. The issue is that she is trying to achieve some standard that cannot be achieved. 

Any critiques of the film that don't explore the male gaze which the film puts on a screen to a silly and absurd parody of the idea or the idea of disassociation also seems odd to me.

This is a pretty stiff read and seems like something that would be done by a 1st/2nd year college student for the college paper. It feels more like a homework assignment than a personal view of a film. 


There's no personal perspective or a sense of author personality. People prefer to read reviews by specific writers not just cause they agree with their taste, but because they enjoy their writing even if they don't agree with their take. It's not "bad," it's just bland and forgettable. You don't have to make it all about you, but if there's no you in the review I might as well read the wiki about it and an AI generated aggregate review.


I'd try to lessen the authoritative voice that suggests objectiveness and tighten up the writing. You spend a lot of time repeating yourself in what seems to be an attempt to solidify a point.


The paragraph:


"However, its two hour runtime feels too long for this kind of film despite its strong ending. There are certain scenes that overtly repeats information shown before and its constant use of narration how impactful it maybe to the characters feels unnecessary, yes we already know what’s happening and what you are showing, you don’t need to show it again."



Could be:


"However, at two hours this film is too long. Scenes begin to repeat themselves and the narration begins to feel redundant. Yes, we already know what's happening. You don't need to show it again."


It feels like youre wordy because you're afraid it won't seem "professional" if you're not. You dont need to justify and explain every point you make. It reads as though youre not just asserting your opinion but also trying to defend it. Just make your point and move on.


In Stephen King's book "On Writing" he has a really good self-editing tip the goes something like: the second draft is the first draft minus 10%. 



Another tip I have: read your review out loud to yourself. It's a great way to realize that even though you got down all the information and ideas you wanted it might be at the expense of clarity. You'll also quickly realize if you're being long winded. It's easy to keep writing and forget where the sentence or paragraph began by the time you're at its end. The amount of time I've read out my own stuff and was either confused, annoyed, or bored by the time I finished saying it is more than I'd like to admit.


Like I said, it's not a bad review. It's just a bit bland and longwinded. I'd just tighten up your writing and put more of yourself in there!
